limitations: Source observations and API research are real; business purpose, WSDL provenance, quantity authority, locations, custom-field ownership and special-date meaning remain unconfirmed.
No customer decisions, reviewer identities or Shopify IDs were fabricated. No live ERP/Shopify requests were executed.
This is a proposed design for review. It is not a production-ready request or a confirmed business specification.

mappings.proposed_rule: Parse as an integer and preserve zero. Propose name=available only if this is authoritative sellable stock. Confirm quantity basis and location; never copy a combined total to every location.
mappings.reason: The XML supplies integer-like quantities per SKU; Shopify accepts a quantity for an inventory item and location.

mappings.proposed_rule: Search using the source SKU with API search escaping. Require exactly one exact SKU match and use its returned inventoryItemId. No match or duplicates go to exception review; the SKU string is not a Shopify ID.
mappings.reason: SKU is the matching key in the source; Shopify supports searching inventory items by SKU.

mappings.proposed_rule: Propose a single_line_text_field on the resolved variant. Preserve populated text exactly. Empty means no message in this sample; agree whether updates omit or clear it. This proposal does not enable storefront display automatically.
mappings.reason: This source availability message can be retained as custom text; it has no equivalent native quantity input.

mappings.proposed_rule: Parse only true/false and serialize the boolean as a string for the metafield value. Do not map directly to availableForSale. Use for comparison/reporting unless storefront behavior is explicitly agreed.
mappings.reason: A custom boolean can preserve the source flag without pretending to write Shopify’s calculated storefront availability.

mappings.proposed_rule: Preserve the external string in a proposed single_line_text_field on the resolved variant, or product if ownership is confirmed at product level. Resolve ownerId through a verified identity lookup; do not construct a Shopify GID from this value.
mappings.reason: The external product reference equals SKU in this sample, but that does not establish a Shopify ID relationship.

mappings.proposed_rule: After clarification, normalize valid dates with an agreed timezone. Hold 2049-12-31 for review; do not present it as a delivery promise or invent a sentinel conversion. The proposed custom key is not a native Shopify availability date.
mappings.reason: A date_time metafield is a possible destination, but timezone and the special future date are unresolved.

mappings.proposed_rule: If downstream consumers need the classification, preserve the raw code in a proposed single_line_text_field. Otherwise propose exclusion after analyst confirmation. Do not convert N into Shopify productType or a product category.
mappings.reason: The code N is observed, but its meaning and whether Shopify needs it are unknown.

observations.text: Nine source records contain seven XML business fields. SKU and WebProductId match within this sample; that is an observation, not a confirmed identity rule.

Per-SKU quantity, stock flags and availability dates suggest an availability snapshot. Inventory synchronization is therefore proposed conditionally; the interface’s actual purpose and inventory authority are still unconfirmed.
custom.* destinations are proposed metafield definitions. They are not built-in Shopify attributes and are not claimed to exist in the customer’s store.
The excerpt is missing two closing tags. A verified closing-tag-only copy supports extraction without changing original values. WSDL provenance remains unconfirmed.
Official 2026-07 input documentation uses changeFromQuantity. Some mutation examples still show compareQuantity. Validate the deployed schema before implementation; no live store call was made.

summary: Five concrete mappings proposed from the supplied XML, plus two candidate mappings needing a business decision. The design uses SKU lookup, conditional inventory updates and clearly identified custom fields. No customer decisions or Shopify store identities have been assumed.
